subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should omitted `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` remain a legacy session heuristic distinct from explicit `minimal`/`standard`/`full`, or should the tier names become the actual defaults?
rationale: The choice affects upgrade compatibility and whether setting an explicit default can drop hook-loaded context, so automation should not decide the permanent public config contract.

options.title: Keep Legacy Omitted Mode
options.body: Preserve current no-override behavior, but make the resolver/docs/schema/help state that omitted config is a distinct compatibility mode and explicit tiers are opt-in.

options.title: Make Defaults Real Tiers
options.body: Route omitted config through the tier allowlists so default main, subagent, and cron behavior exactly matches the documented tier names, accepting the compatibility impact only with maintainer approval.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Context Design
options.body: Pause this PR behind the broader bootstrap/context-selection proposals if maintainers want one unified selector instead of a new tier knob now.

recommendation.title: Keep Legacy Omitted Mode
recommendation.body: Preserve current no-override behavior, but make the resolver/docs/schema/help state that omitted config is a distinct compatibility mode and explicit tiers are opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the earlier subagent bootstrap limiting behavior and is the strongest history-backed owner for the config/default compatibility decision.
